mechanism_note: Birth weight category is a mediator, not a classical confounder — it lies on the causal pathway from maternal smoking to infant mortality (smoking causes low birth weight, which causes elevated mortality). Conditioning on birth weight (stratifying) opens a collider path: among LBW infants, smoker babies are 'selected in' via a milder mechanism (growth restriction) while non-smoker LBW babies are more likely to have serious congenital causes. This creates the paradox: smokers appear to have better LBW survival not because smoking is protective, but because the comparison groups differ in unobserved severity. IsSignFlip=TRUE, RI=0.5 → type-B (partial reversal: smokers win LBW stratum, non-smokers win NBW, non-smokers win pooled).
